name: H.L. Hunley
location: Warren Lasch Conservation Center, North Charleston, SC
description: The first submarine in history to sink an enemy warship, the Hunley attacked the USS Housatonic in 1864 during the Civil War. Raised from the seafloor in 2000, she is now on display at the Warren Lasch Conservation Center undergoing ongoing conservation.

name: USS Albacore
location: Albacore Park, Portsmouth, NH
description: Launched in 1953, Albacore pioneered the teardrop hull design that became standard on virtually every submarine built since. Though she carried no weapons, her hydrodynamic research transformed submarine design worldwide.

name: USS Batfish
location: Muskogee War Memorial Park, Muskogee, OK
description: Batfish achieved one of the most remarkable feats of the Pacific War — sinking three Japanese submarines in 76 hours in February 1945. She is Oklahoma's only submarine museum.

name: USS Becuna
location: Independence Seaport Museum, Philadelphia, PA
description: A Pacific War veteran, Becuna completed five war patrols and is now part of the Independence Seaport Museum's historic ship collection, moored alongside the cruiser Olympia at Penn's Landing.

name: USS Blueback
location: Oregon Museum of Science and Industry, Portland, OR
description: The last diesel-electric submarine built for the U.S. Navy, Blueback was decommissioned in 1990. She appeared in the film The Hunt for Red October and is now open for tours at the Oregon Museum of Science and Industry.

name: USS Bowfin
location: Pearl Harbor Historic Sites, Honolulu, HI
description: Known as the "Pearl Harbor Avenger," Bowfin sank 44 enemy vessels during WWII. Located adjacent to the USS Arizona Memorial, she is one of the best-preserved and most visited submarine museums in the world.

name: USS Cavalla
location: Galveston Naval Museum, Seawolf Park, Galveston, TX
description: On her first war patrol in June 1944, Cavalla sank the Japanese aircraft carrier Shokaku — a veteran of the Pearl Harbor attack. She is displayed alongside the destroyer escort USS Stewart at Seawolf Park.

name: USS Cobia
location: Wisconsin Maritime Museum, Manitowoc, WI
description: Cobia is a near-sister of the 28 submarines built at the Manitowoc Shipbuilding Company — the only inland shipyard to build fleet submarines during WWII. She completed six Pacific war patrols and is the centerpiece of the Wisconsin Maritime Museum.

name: USS Cod
location: Cleveland, OH
description: One of the most intact WWII submarines in existence, Cod completed seven Pacific war patrols and performed the only international submarine-to-submarine rescue in history. She is a National Historic Landmark moored on the Lake Erie waterfront.

name: USS Croaker
location: Buffalo and Erie County Naval & Military Park, Buffalo, NY
description: A Pacific War veteran that completed six war patrols, Croaker is now part of the Buffalo Naval & Military Park — home to one of the largest collections of warships on the Great Lakes.

name: USS Dolphin
location: Maritime Museum of San Diego, San Diego, CA
description: The deepest-diving operational submarine ever built, Dolphin set a depth record exceeding 3,000 feet. She represents the cutting edge of Cold War-era submarine research and is part of the Maritime Museum of San Diego's historic fleet.

name: USS Drum
location: Battleship Memorial Park, Mobile, AL
description: The first fleet submarine commissioned after Pearl Harbor, Drum completed 13 war patrols and sank 15 Japanese vessels totaling over 80,000 tons. She is displayed alongside the battleship USS Alabama at Mobile Bay.

name: USS Growler
location: Intrepid Sea, Air & Space Museum, New York, NY
description: The only American guided missile submarine open to the public, Growler carried nuclear-tipped Regulus missiles during the Cold War. She is displayed alongside the aircraft carrier Intrepid at Pier 86 in Manhattan.

name: USS Lionfish
location: Battleship Cove, Fall River, MA
description: Commissioned in late 1944, Lionfish completed one Pacific war patrol before the war's end. Remarkably preserved with much of her original equipment intact, she is part of the Battleship Cove complex alongside the battleship USS Massachusetts.

name: USS Nautilus
location: Submarine Force Museum, Groton, CT
description: The world's first nuclear-powered vessel, Nautilus was commissioned in 1954 and became the first submarine to complete a submerged transit of the North Pole in 1958. She is a National Historic Landmark at the Submarine Force Museum — home of the official U.S. Navy submarine museum.

name: USS Pampanito
location: Pier 45, Fisherman's Wharf, San Francisco, CA
description: World War II fleet submarine and National Historic Landmark, berthed at Pier 45 in San Francisco. Pampanito conducted six war patrols in the Pacific and participated in the rescue of Allied POWs from Japanese transport ships.

name: USS Razorback
location: Arkansas Inland Maritime Museum, North Little Rock, AR
description: One of the longest-serving combat submarines in history, Razorback served in both the U.S. and Turkish navies for a combined 56 years. She is moored on the Arkansas River at the Arkansas Inland Maritime Museum.

name: USS Requin
location: Kamin Science Center, Pittsburgh, PA
description: Commissioned in 1945, Requin was converted to the Navy's first radar picket submarine in 1947. She is moored on the Allegheny River at the Kamin Science Center — the only submarine museum in western Pennsylvania.

name: USS Silversides
location: Great Lakes Naval Memorial and Museum, Muskegon, MI
description: One of the most decorated submarines of WWII, Silversides completed 14 war patrols and sank 23 ships for over 90,000 tons — third highest of any U.S. submarine. She is a National Historic Landmark open year-round at the Great Lakes Naval Memorial and Museum.

name: USS Torsk
location: Historic Ships in Baltimore, Baltimore, MD
description: Torsk fired the last torpedo of WWII, sinking a Japanese coastal defense vessel on August 14, 1945 — the final day of the war. She is part of the Historic Ships in Baltimore collection alongside the Civil War sloop USS Constellation.
